note: queue_unique provides the service queue_unique.database (UniqueQueueDatabaseFactory -> UniqueDatabaseQueue extends DatabaseQueue) which stores items in its own 'queue_unique' table with a unique 'hash' key; createItem() returns FALSE and stores nothing on a duplicate. No config, no schema, no permissions, no admin UI, no module-specific Drush. Medium/hard cases are grounded in real live queue state: setup/reset scripts create/empty unique queues (qu_*) via the service and count rows in the queue_unique table (verify/introspection). Item counts are read from the live queue_unique table keyed by queue name.

evals.prompt: In Drupal, how do I get a queue that rejects duplicate items using the queue_unique module, and how do I know when an item was rejected as a duplicate?
evals.expected_output: Use the service: $queue = \Drupal::service('queue_unique.database')->get('name'); (or set $settings['queue_service_name'] = 'queue_unique.database' in settings.php and use the normal queue service). createItem() returns FALSE (and stores nothing) when the item is a duplicate.

evals.prompt: With the queue_unique module, what happens when you try to add an item that is already in the queue?
evals.expected_output: The duplicate is not added; createItem() returns FALSE. Uniqueness is enforced by a unique key on a hash column in the 'queue_unique' table (an IntegrityConstraintViolationException is caught and FALSE returned).

evals.prompt: The queue_unique module mentions a way to make queue workers use unique queues automatically on cron by replacing the core QueueFactory. What queue-name prefix do you use, and what class replaces the core queue service?
evals.expected_output: Replace the core 'queue' service with Drupal\queue_unique\QueueFactory; then any queue name prefixed 'queue_unique/' (e.g. queue_unique/mymodule_work, or a @QueueWorker plugin id with that prefix) is served by queue_unique.database with the prefix stripped.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site there is a unique queue named qu_known (managed by the queue_unique module). Inspect the live site and state how many items are currently in that queue.
evals.expected_output: qu_known has 2 items. (Three inserts were attempted but one was an exact duplicate and was rejected by the unique queue.) Read via the queue: \Drupal::service('queue_unique.database')->get('qu_known')->numberOfItems().

evals.prompt: This site has two unique queues, qu_alpha and qu_beta, both managed by queue_unique. Inspect the live queues and state which one currently holds more items.
evals.expected_output: qu_beta holds more (3 items vs qu_alpha's 1). Compare numberOfItems() of each unique queue, or count rows per name in the queue_unique table.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, add an item to a queue named qu_task using the queue_unique module's unique database queue (NOT the core queue table). Any payload is fine. Apply it to the live site.
evals.expected_output: The queue_unique table has at least one row with name=qu_task, e.g. \Drupal::service('queue_unique.database')->get('qu_task')->createItem($data).

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, add the SAME data item to a unique queue named qu_dup (managed by queue_unique) two times. Because the queue only accepts unique items, only one copy should end up stored. Apply it to the live site.
evals.expected_output: After inserting an identical payload twice via queue_unique.database->get('qu_dup'), exactly one row exists for name=qu_dup (the second createItem() returned FALSE).
